correctness.rationale: Every feasible allocation satisfies two exact Walsh Rayleigh-quotient averaged bounds. The min of the bounds optimizes exactly at the claimed matching-budget amount when t<d, while the singleton bound is sharp for t>=d. Direct complete Walsh diagonalization realizes each optimum. Equality in test-character Rayleigh inequalities forces eigenvector identities, giving unique all-edge weights for t!=d and an exactly characterized one-dimensional face at t=d, including boundary endpoints. Test script passed 2310 checks but is not treated as proof.

originality.rationale: The precise two-edge-class priced folded-hypercube fastest-diffusion phase transition and its complete all-edge-variable optimizer classification were not found in the inspected sources. The foundational continuous-time FMMP SDP and unweighted Walsh cube spectra are explicitly prior art; the added global equality rigidity and flat critical optimal face are specific mathematical contributions. The comparison is best-knowledge, not proof of historical uniqueness.

value.rationale: A natural nonlocal augmentation of a high-dimensional interconnection graph has an exact linear-in-dimension price cutoff determining whether all antipodal links should be bought. The theorem classifies all independently variable optimizers, including surprising exact rigidity of every critical allocation and a flat transition face, rather than merely exhibiting orbit-constant candidates. This supplies a usable explicit resource-design rule not directly present in the foundational general framework.
